purpose: Public learning map for Bionic Banker AI, wallet-risk, agent, and evidence concepts.
privacy_boundary: Definitions and learning notes only. No keys, IPs, client data, wallet secrets, or infrastructure details.

concepts.plain_definition: Software that performs tasks that normally require reasoning, pattern recognition, language understanding, prediction, or decision support.
concepts.why_it_matters: AI is the umbrella. The useful question is what task it helps, what evidence it uses, and where a human still makes the final call.

concepts.plain_definition: A language model trained to read and generate text. It can summarize, classify, draft, reason over context, and call tools when connected to a workflow.
concepts.why_it_matters: LLMs are useful when they are grounded in sources, tests, citations, and approval gates. Without that, they can sound confident while being wrong.

concepts.plain_definition: A vision-language model that can reason over images and text together.
concepts.why_it_matters: VLMs are useful for screenshots, chart review, UI QA, document inspection, and visual review workflows.

concepts.plain_definition: An AI workflow that can observe state, choose a next step, use tools, write outputs, and wait for human approval when the action matters.
concepts.why_it_matters: The agent is not just the model. The agent is the loop around the model: memory, tools, rules, tests, logs, and gates.

concepts.plain_definition: A pattern where a model asks to use a defined tool, such as search, a database query, a file read, or a calculation, instead of guessing.
concepts.why_it_matters: Tool calling turns a model from a text generator into a controlled worker. The boundary is the tool contract.

concepts.plain_definition: A developer framework for connecting language models to tools, prompts, memory, retrieval, and workflow steps.
concepts.why_it_matters: LangChain is one way to structure AI apps. The value is not name-dropping it. The value is showing tool boundaries and testable behavior.

concepts.plain_definition: A graph-based framework for building stateful agent workflows where steps can branch, loop, pause, and resume.
concepts.why_it_matters: It maps well to real systems because real work is not always one straight chain. There are retries, approvals, validators, and fallbacks.

concepts.plain_definition: Retrieval augmented generation. The model retrieves relevant source material first, then writes an answer using that material.
concepts.why_it_matters: RAG is how you reduce guessing. The question becomes: what did the model retrieve, can we cite it, and was the source trustworthy?

concepts.plain_definition: Numeric representations of text, images, or other data that help software compare meaning instead of exact words.
concepts.why_it_matters: Embeddings make search smarter. They help find related ideas even when the wording is different.

concepts.plain_definition: Model Context Protocol. A standard pattern for letting AI systems connect to tools and data sources through defined interfaces.
concepts.why_it_matters: MCP matters because agents need clean boundaries. A tool should say what it can do, what inputs it accepts, and what output it returns.

concepts.plain_definition: Role-based access control. A way to decide who or what is allowed to perform each action.
concepts.why_it_matters: RBAC is essential for regulated AI because not every agent should be allowed to do every action.

concepts.plain_definition: A record of what happened, when it happened, what tool or person did it, and what evidence supported it.
concepts.why_it_matters: If a system cannot explain its own actions later, it is not ready for serious finance, healthcare, or compliance work.

concepts.plain_definition: The ability to see whether a system is alive, what it is doing, what failed, and what changed over time.
concepts.why_it_matters: Invisible automation is risky. Observable automation can be trusted, debugged, and improved.

concepts.plain_definition: A small status signal that shows a system woke up, ran, and wrote its latest state.
concepts.why_it_matters: A heartbeat does not prove a system is perfect. It proves the loop is still alive and observable.

concepts.plain_definition: Anti-money laundering. The work of detecting, investigating, and preventing financial activity that may be tied to crime or sanctions risk.
concepts.why_it_matters: AML is where finance, data, rules, and judgment meet. Good AML systems explain why a transaction looks risky.

concepts.plain_definition: A system flags something as risky, but after review it is not actually risky.
concepts.why_it_matters: False positives matter because they waste review time. In compliance, accuracy is not only detection. It is also how much noise the system creates.

concepts.plain_definition: Ethereum Virtual Machine. The execution environment used by Ethereum and many compatible blockchain networks.
concepts.why_it_matters: EVM compatibility lets one wallet-risk tool support many chains with similar address and transaction patterns.

concepts.plain_definition: A system for running, scaling, and managing containers across machines.
concepts.why_it_matters: Kubernetes is useful when a project needs deployment discipline, service health, scaling, and reproducible operations.

concepts.plain_definition: A way to package an app and its dependencies into a container that can run consistently across environments.
concepts.why_it_matters: Docker makes projects easier to test, share, and deploy because the environment is part of the package.

concepts.plain_definition: A graphics processing unit. In AI, GPUs are used to run many calculations in parallel.
concepts.why_it_matters: GPUs matter for model training, image models, local inference, and workloads where parallel math is the bottleneck.

guides.title: Top 5 ways to learn AI by building
items: Pick one small problem and make the output visible.
Log every model input, tool call, and final output.
Add one independent check before trusting the result.
Turn the project into a page someone else can read.
Repeat with a slightly harder workflow.

guides.title: Top 5 ways to prompt an agent
items: Give it the goal, not only the task.
Name what it is allowed to do and what it must not do.
Make it write a checkpoint when work becomes important.
Keep irreversible actions behind a human gate.

guides.title: Top 5 rules for visible evidence
items: Show the artifact, not the private workspace.
Use links, screenshots, tests, and notes as the evidence path.
Avoid secrets, client data, and unsupported claims.

stack_radar.why_2026_teams_care: People understand technical work faster when they can inspect a working page instead of only reading claims.
stack_radar.learn_here: Use the Systems and Reports pages to move from a working page to the numbers, limits, and next question.
stack_radar.reader_question: Can someone understand the path without reading the full project archive?

stack_radar.why_2026_teams_care: RAG is only useful when retrieval is traceable, cited, and evaluated against expected answers.
stack_radar.learn_here: Study RAG, embeddings, audit logs, and observability together instead of as separate words.
stack_radar.reader_question: How do AI answers cite sources instead of only sounding confident?

stack_radar.why_2026_teams_care: AI teams need to know what changed, what failed, and whether a model or agent got better or worse.
stack_radar.learn_here: Use the Reports page to connect benchmark numbers, limitations, and system health.
stack_radar.reader_question: How do teams know an AI workflow improved instead of only changed?

stack_radar.why_2026_teams_care: Regulated workflows need role boundaries, approval gates, trace events, and reviewable tool use.
stack_radar.learn_here: Connect RBAC, audit logs, tool calling, MCP, and approval gates as one rule pattern.
stack_radar.reader_question: What should an AI agent be allowed to do by itself?

stack_radar.why_2026_teams_care: A demonstration becomes stronger when it can be packaged, health-checked, monitored, and redeployed predictably.
stack_radar.learn_here: Use Docker and Kubernetes as the path from local demonstration to reliable service behavior.
stack_radar.reader_question: What makes an AI demonstration repeatable, observable, and easier to trust?
